AbstractText.Label: CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common cause of anovulation. It may also negatively affect the endometrium, which could lead to implantation failure and proliferative aberrations.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Our objective was to study sex hormone receptors in the endometrium of women with PCOS.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: This is a cross-sectional study and lifestyle intervention.

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Clinical and laboratory research unit was undertaken at a university hospital.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Twenty overweight/obese women fulfilling all three PCOS criteria (anovulation, hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovaries), 10 body mass index-matched regularly menstruating controls, 11 normal-weight women with PCOS, and 11 normal-weight controls.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Intervention for this study included dietary management and physical exercise.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: mRNA levels and immunostaining of estrogen receptor α (ERα) and β (ERβ), nongenomic estrogen receptor α36 (ERα36), and G-protein-coupled estrogen receptor-1 (GPER), and the androgen receptor (AR) on cycle days 6-8 and cycle days 21-23.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Before intervention, mRNA levels of ERα, ERα36, and the ERα/ERβ mRNA ratio were lower in proliferative endometrium of overweight/obese PCOS women compared with controls (P < .05). After intervention, ERα protein and the ERα/ERβ protein ratio in proliferative endometrium increased and were higher in PCOS women with improved menstrual function than in those without improvement (P < .05). In the subgroup of PCOS women with restored ovulation, only higher protein levels of GPER were found in secretory endometrium (P < .01). However, PCOS women who remained anovulatory had higher protein levels of ERα, GPER, and AR on cycle days 21-23 than controls (P < .05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Lifestyle intervention alters, but does not fully restore, ER and AR expression in proliferative and secretory endometrium of obese women with PCOS.
